correctness.rationale: Burek §4 provides all six local equations. At v=0 and ∞ the principal part is −z²+4s⁴−q; at v=±1 and ±i it is 4z²−16s⁴−q in the given coordinates (swap the two factor functions for ±i). The weights of x,y,s,z are 1,1,1,2 and all corrections have weight greater than 4. By Euler's identity any common projective zero of q_x,q_y would be a multiple projective root of q, which has four distinct linear factors. Their length is 3·3 as a regular sequence of cubics; the z and s factors of the principal Jacobian have lengths 1 and 3. Semiquasihomogeneous invariance gives μ=27 for the exact germs without claiming analytic equivalence to the initial forms. The Milnor fiber of an isolated complex threefold hypersurface germ is a bouquet of 27 three-spheres, so χ=−26. Burek's 9 is for a surface fiber. Frozen verify.py and its recorded output cover the binary quartic and the weight check at v=0; the other five points were checked from the source, not from a replay of that script. No global smoothing follows.
